title: Top tips for reducing cancer risk through lifestyle changes | Daily Sabah
summary: Registered dietitian Çisem Gündüz outlines lifestyle and nutrition strategies to lower cancer risk, highlighting that 30–50% of cancers are preventable. Adopting a Mediterranean diet, eating 400g of fruits and vegetables daily, regular physical activity, managing stress, avoiding smoking and limiting alcohol reduce risk. Emphasizes antioxidants, omega-3s, fiber, fermented foods for gut health, and warns against processed meats and high glycemic foods. Specific foods like garlic, yogurt, tomatoes and cruciferous vegetables offer protective benefits.
content:
Cancer is one of the leading causes of death worldwide, but what if simple lifestyle changes could significantly lower the risk? Dietitian Çisem Gündüz offers valuable insights into how nutrition and lifestyle can play a significant role in cancer prevention. According to Gündüz, individuals who adopt a Mediterranean diet can reduce their risk of developing cancer by up to 20%. She also highlights specific foods, such as yogurt, pickles, garlic and onions, known for their immune-boosting properties and overall health benefits.

Gündüz emphasizes the importance of nutrition and lifestyle in reducing cancer risk. Studies from the World Cancer Research Fund (WCRF) and the American Institute for Cancer Research (AICR) show that 30-50% of cancers can be prevented. Nutrition is one of the most significant modifiable risk factors in this regard.

According to Harvard Medical School, consuming at least 400 grams of fruits and vegetables daily helps protect against certain types of cancer, including stomach and colon cancer. Gündüz also references studies showing that individuals who closely follow a Mediterranean diet can reduce their overall cancer risk by 10-20%. This diet is rich in antioxidants, anti-inflammatory compounds and fiber – all of which play a positive role in cancer prevention and treatment. Foods such as whole grains, legumes, and fiber-rich vegetables offer particularly strong protection against colon cancer.

Regular physical activity is another key factor in reducing cancer risk. Gündüz highlights clinical research suggesting that engaging in 150 minutes of moderate exercise per week can lower the risk of several types of cancer, especially breast and colon cancer. Furthermore, smoking is responsible for 85% of lung cancer cases, while alcohol consumption has been linked to an increased risk of breast, liver, and esophageal cancers.

Gündüz mentions melatonin, a hormone that supports cell renewal and plays a key role in regulating the body’s circadian rhythm. Chronic stress, which suppresses the immune system, can accelerate the development of certain types of cancer. She also emphasizes the importance of antioxidants in preventing DNA damage, which is crucial for cancer prevention. Vitamin C, vitamin E, selenium, polyphenols, and flavonoids can all help reduce cancer risk. Specifically, lycopene and carotenoids – found in tomatoes, carrots, sweet potatoes and red peppers – protect against DNA damage and reduce inflammation. Clinical studies have shown that high lycopene intake can reduce prostate cancer risk by 30%.

Strengthening gut health is essential for supporting the immune system. Gündüz recommends foods like yogurt, pickles, garlic, and onions, which enhance gut flora and improve immune function, further helping to reduce cancer risk.

Broccoli, cauliflower, cabbage, and turnips contain enzymes that neutralize carcinogens. Omega-3 fatty acids, found in salmon, flax seeds, and walnuts, can also slow cancer cell proliferation by stabilizing cell membranes. Additionally, prebiotics and probiotics, which strengthen gut flora, support immunity and lower cancer risk. Foods rich in flavonoids and polyphenols – such as green tea, pomegranate, and red grapes – aid in cell renewal and protect healthy cell functions.

Gündüz also warns against consuming processed meats, such as salami, sausage and pepperoni, which the World Health Organization (WHO) classifies as carcinogenic (Group 1). High glycemic index foods, which increase insulin resistance, have been linked to various cancers, particularly those of the pancreas, breast and colon.

markdown_content:
## Overview

Cancer is one of the leading causes of death worldwide, but what if simple lifestyle changes could significantly lower the risk? Dietitian Çisem Gündüz offers valuable insights into how nutrition and lifestyle can play a significant role in cancer prevention. According to Gündüz, individuals who adopt a Mediterranean diet can reduce their risk of developing cancer by up to 20%. She also highlights specific foods, such as yogurt, pickles, garlic and onions, known for their immune-boosting properties and overall health benefits.

## Evidence and statistics

Gündüz emphasizes the importance of nutrition and lifestyle in reducing cancer risk. Studies from the World Cancer Research Fund (WCRF) and the American Institute for Cancer Research (AICR) show that 30–50% of cancers can be prevented. Nutrition is one of the most significant modifiable risk factors in this regard.

According to Harvard Medical School, consuming at least 400 grams of fruits and vegetables daily helps protect against certain types of cancer, including stomach and colon cancer. Gündüz also references studies showing that individuals who closely follow a Mediterranean diet can reduce their overall cancer risk by 10–20%. This diet is rich in antioxidants, anti-inflammatory compounds and fiber — all of which play a positive role in cancer prevention and treatment. Foods such as whole grains, legumes, and fiber-rich vegetables offer particularly strong protection against colon cancer.

## Physical activity and other lifestyle factors

Regular physical activity is another key factor in reducing cancer risk. Gündüz highlights clinical research suggesting that engaging in 150 minutes of moderate exercise per week can lower the risk of several types of cancer, especially breast and colon cancer. Furthermore, smoking is responsible for 85% of lung cancer cases, while alcohol consumption has been linked to an increased risk of breast, liver, and esophageal cancers.

Gündüz mentions melatonin, a hormone that supports cell renewal and plays a key role in regulating the body’s circadian rhythm. Chronic stress, which suppresses the immune system, can accelerate the development of certain types of cancer. She also emphasizes the importance of antioxidants in preventing DNA damage, which is crucial for cancer prevention.

## Key foods and compounds that may reduce cancer risk

- Vitamins and antioxidants:
  - Vitamin C, vitamin E, selenium, polyphenols and flavonoids can all help reduce cancer risk.
- Carotenoids and lycopene:
  - Lycopene and carotenoids — found in tomatoes, carrots, sweet potatoes and red peppers — protect against DNA damage and reduce inflammation. Clinical studies have shown that high lycopene intake can reduce prostate cancer risk by 30%.
- Fiber and whole foods:
  - Whole grains, legumes and fiber-rich vegetables offer strong protection, particularly against colon cancer.
- Omega-3 fatty acids:
  - Found in salmon, flax seeds and walnuts; may slow cancer cell proliferation by stabilizing cell membranes.
- Flavonoid- and polyphenol-rich foods:
  - Green tea, pomegranate and red grapes aid in cell renewal and help protect healthy cell functions.
- Cruciferous vegetables:
  - Broccoli, cauliflower, cabbage and turnips contain enzymes that neutralize carcinogens.

## Gut health and immune support

Strengthening gut health is essential for supporting the immune system. Gündüz recommends foods like yogurt, pickles, garlic and onions, which enhance gut flora and improve immune function, further helping to reduce cancer risk. Additionally, prebiotics and probiotics, which strengthen gut flora, support immunity and lower cancer risk.

## Foods and behaviors to avoid

Gündüz also warns against consuming processed meats, such as salami, sausage and pepperoni, which the World Health Organization (WHO) classifies as carcinogenic (Group 1). High glycemic index foods, which increase insulin resistance, have been linked to various cancers, particularly those of the pancreas, breast and colon.

## Practical takeaways

- Adopt a Mediterranean-style diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, legumes, nuts, olive oil and fish.
- Aim for at least 400 grams of fruits and vegetables daily.
- Get 150 minutes of moderate exercise per week.
- Reduce or avoid processed meats and high–glycemic index foods.
- Support gut health with probiotic and prebiotic foods like yogurt, pickles, garlic and onions.
- Prioritize stress management, adequate sleep and other behaviors that support circadian rhythm and immune function.
